Hi Diego,

Thanks for the demo last week — Veridian's product and your latency profile look promising. Our procurement/legal team has a quick question about the transfer mechanism before we proceed: we are a data controller and plan to send de-identified and limited PHI (HIPAA-covered) to Redwood's hosted inference (Redwood will act as processor). For contract execution we typically use the EU SCCs.

Two specific asks:
- Can you confirm which SCCs module you expect us to sign (Controller -> Processor vs Processor -> Processor)? We want to avoid a later rework.
- We also need an evidence pack for the security controls referenced in the DPA (encryption, KMS, subprocessor list, SOC 2 scope). Can you share a draft SCCs annex/annexes and an estimated timeline for execution (we have an internal go/no-go review next Thursday).

Appreciate a short answer so we can schedule the review.

Thanks,
Jules Martin
Head of Partnerships
Veridian Health

Subject: Fwd: SCCs / module selection question for hosted inference (Veridian -> Redwood)

Laura / Marissa — forwarding Veridian's note. Short read.

My take (quick):
- This is a classic controller -> processor relationship (Veridian is controller, Redwood hosted inference is processor) so Module 2 of the EU SCCs is the expected path. UK needs the UK Addendum.
- Because they call out HIPAA-covered data, we should:
  1) Add HIPAA-specific assurances in the DPA / Annex 2 (technical controls) — specifically: customer-owned KMS, encryption at rest+in transit, logging retention for 12 months (or configurable), and a written list of subprocessors with 30-day notice.
  2) Provide a short evidence bundle: SOC 2 Type II summary, network encryption diagram, KMS architecture note, and a redacted subprocessor registry.
- I'll attach a Module2 draft with proposed Annex language for HIPAA. Can Legal confirm there are no unusual obligations we should refuse (data minimization, onward transfers to third-country subprocessors, etc.)? Marissa, can you prepare the evidence pack items from Security? We should aim to send Veridian a DocuSign-ready SCCs package by Wed EOD to hit their review on Thursday.

Attaching: SCCs_Module2_draft_v3.docx

Thanks,
Diego
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: SCCs / module selection question for hosted inference (Veridian -> Redwood)

Diego — thanks for the summary.

Legal confirms: Module 2 (Controller -> Processor) is the correct EU SCCs module for the standard hosted inference relationship. UK transfers should be handled with the UK Addendum in addition to the EU SCCs (we attach the addendum language into the same package).

A few legal points / redlines to keep in mind for this customer because of HIPAA mention:
- Include explicit language in Annex II (technical and organizational measures) referencing encryption standards (AES-256 at rest, TLS1.3 in transit), key ownership/management (customer KMS supported; we can offer Redwood-managed KMS only with documented limitations).
- Add a clause for 'assistance with data subject requests' tailored to controller obligations.
- For subprocessors: we can provide a current registry and commit to 30-day notice. Do not promise 'no-third-country subprocessors' — we should instead commit to notice and appropriate SCCs downstream.
- Consider a short DPIA statement in the annex: identify the types of data classes processed (pseudonymized PHI, inference prompts), and note retention/erasure controls. This will help their privacy team.

Timeline: Legal can finalize the redlines by Tue EOD if Security provides the evidence pack items today. After Legal sign-off we can produce a DocuSign envelope.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection | Redwood Inference
